title: EarthLink identifies an eight-month predictor set for Atlantic Niño hindcasts
summary: On an open-ended climate-analysis task, the EarthLink agent autonomously selected two Atlantic-internal predictors for the summer ATL3 index at an eight-month lead: the SON-to-November tendency of the equatorial east–west sea-level-pressure gradient and November western-equatorial-Atlantic sea level as a thermocline-tilt proxy. Rolling-origin hindcasts for 1995–2023 achieved a temporal correlation of about 0.46, above persistence (~0.13) and ENSO-only baselines. The paper proposes a Kelvin-wave/Bjerknes-feedback explanation for the association.
ai_technology: EarthLink multi-agent AI research system based on foundation language models and climate data/tools
organization: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory; Fudan University; Institute of Atmospheric Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology; Ocean University of China; Columbia University

evidence.tested: On an open-ended climate-analysis task, the EarthLink agent autonomously selected two Atlantic-internal predictors for the summer ATL3 index at an eight-month lead: the SON-to-November tendency of the equatorial east–west sea-level-pressure gradient and November western-equatorial-Atlantic sea level as a thermocline-tilt proxy.
evidence.unknown: This is an unrefereed arXiv preprint and a retrospective rolling-origin hindcast from one observational/reanalysis data setup. The physical pathway is an AI-generated, testable hypothesis that the authors explicitly say requires further validation; the source does not establish a causal mechanism or demonstrated prospective operational forecast. Skill is ~0.46 and falls short of the authors’ 0.5 target.
evidence.ai_role: Given an open-ended Atlantic Niño precursor problem, EarthLink autonomously planned analyses, generated code, tested predictors using regression models, reviewed literature and synthesized a physical mechanism. The paper states the proposed AI-generated hypothesis needs further validation.
